And Elena, are there any other closing controls beyond the segregated reserve that Treasury requires?

transcript.text: Thanks, Maya. That's an important question. I want to be clear about what I can and can't confirm right now. What I've established from my contract review is the legal requirement: the assignment-consent package for KITE and NORTHSTAR must be signed and in the closing file before closing, regardless of whether their invoices are included or excluded from the pool. That's a firm closing condition. However, I have not yet assessed the practical feasibility of obtaining those consents before June 30, 2026 — I haven't reached out to either customer, and I don't have information about their responsiveness or willingness to consent. So I can't give you a reliable feasibility assessment at this point. What I'd recommend is that we proceed on two parallel tracks: first, plan to close on the reduced $7,200,000 pool as the baseline scenario, since that's certain; and second, I'll initiate outreach to KITE and NORTHSTAR immediately to gauge whether consents can be secured before the closing date. If consents come through in time, we can evaluate whether to expand the pool. If not, the reduced pool closing proceeds without delay. Either way, the signed consent package remains a closing condition — so if we close on the reduced pool without their invoices, we still need those consents signed and filed. I'll upload my full contract review to the transaction folder today so the team has the documentation.
